newsitem.title: UK: Copper holds day's gain in quiet late London.
newsitem.headline: Copper holds day's gain in quiet late London.

text.p: Three-months London Metal Exchange (LME) copper held the day's modest gain registered by the end of the afternoon kerb during later inter-office activity. By 1800 GMT when Comex closed LME copper was bid at $1,942 per tonne.
This compared with a kerb close at $1,936 which was up $11 from Wednesday but down from Thursday's $1,953 best. LME stocks are seen falling tomorrow, traders said.

Latest developments in the Sumitomo Corp scandal did not influence the market much during Thursday. Sumitomo said losses in 10 years of alleged unauthorised trading by Yasuo Hamanaka were $2.6 billion, not the $1.8 billion originally reported.
Most of its uncovered positions have now been liquidated.

Brokerage Rudolf Wolff said in its Evening Metal Report that it expected resistance at $1,950-1,970 to hold but a breach would signal that a run up to $2,000 "could be on the cards". But it noted the market was moving into contango and that there was a well-documented increase in production. Aluminium concluded the kerb at $1,428, a $5 loss, and was bid easier at $1,422 by the later Comex close.
LME stocks are seen rising on Friday while IPAI production data for August is expected to show that output is rising.
